content:
The image shows a handful of soybean seeds held in a palm. Key observations:

- Several seeds show pink to purple discoloration, ranging from small spots to coverage of most of the seed surface
- Some seeds appear normal yellow/tan
- The discoloration appears to extend from the hilum area on some seeds
- No mold or shriveling visible — seeds appear otherwise intact

This matches **Purple_Seed_Stain** very closely: "Infected seeds show pink to purple spots ranging from specks to large blotches covering the entire surface, with discoloration extending from the seed hilum."

The pattern of some seeds heavily stained purple/violet and others normal is classic for this disease. This does not match Phomopsis (which causes cracked, shriveled, moldy seeds) or Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (smoky/mottled coats).
